## What shipped

`EmailProvider` interface, `ProviderSendRequest` + `SendResult` types, `ProviderError` class with `_tag` brand and `isProviderError()` guard, and `createSesAdapter()` factory — all in `src/providers/`. AWS SDK v3 SES adapter uses two send paths: `SendEmailCommand` for standard sends, `SendRawEmailCommand` with hand-built multipart/alternative MIME for List-Unsubscribe bulk sends. `send()` never throws — all errors returned as `{ success: false }`. `validate()` checks env presence only.

## What didn't ship (if anything)

AC-4 (real-credential smoke test) is an operator-gate — requires manual send with live SES credentials.

## Notes / observations

- Factory pattern (`createSesAdapter(config?)`) paid off immediately in the tester — zero `process.env` mutation across 17 ses.test.ts tests. P002 will find the adapter file genuinely copy-paste-able.
- `interface.ts` is pure types but still needs Gate B coverage — a 4-test `interface.test.ts` that imports the types and constructs a conforming object satisfies this cleanly.
- The two-command-path design (SendEmailCommand / SendRawEmailCommand) is the correct AWS SDK v3 approach; `SendEmailCommand` doesn't expose custom headers. MIME construction is ~25 lines and straightforward.
- Lazy `SESClient` construction (built on first `send()` call, not at factory time) is important: `validate()` must be callable on a partially-configured adapter without crashing the SDK constructor. Tester caught a minor mock-capture ordering issue because of this — resolved by capturing `getMockSend()` after `send()` resolves.
